correctness.rationale: All n>=3 with omega(n)<=5 are covered by even prime powers, even mixed support, and odd cases split by 3|psi(n). For even mixed support, 6|psi(n), phi(psi(n))/psi(n)<=1/3 and psi(n)/n<=1152/385, giving 384/385; exact simultaneous equality forces support {2,3,5,7,11}, and exponents at 5,7,11 equal to 1. Conversely psi(2^a3^b*5*7*11)=2^(a+7)3^(b+2), implying equality for all a,b>=1. Even prime powers have ratio 1/2. Odd 3|psi(n) yields <=512/715; odd 3∤psi(n) restricts prime support to 3 or 1 mod 3 and gives <=20480/22971. All strict comparisons are exact fractions. The n=39270 computation psi=124416 and phi=41472 proves six prime support is the next violating layer. Finite integer sieve to n=300000 independently cross-checks but is not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Remark 3.10 of Sándor (2005) proves only even omega<=2 and odd omega<=4 by a psi<=2n sufficient condition; this condition fails at n=2310 with psi/n=1152/385>2. His Remark 3.26 already exhibits n=39270, and OEIS A196200 lists numerical counterexamples; neither establishes the all-size omega<=5 upper bound nor its exact equality family. The 2016 Sándor note concerns power/product inequalities of psi instead. published-finding corpus searches using exact functions, parameters, ratio and conjecture returned no implication-dominating record; nearest indexed work treats different arithmetic functions. Unindexed prior proofs remain a residual risk, so originality is a self-review rather than independent certification.

value.rationale: The object is Sándor's disproved phi(psi(n))<=n conjecture; the mathematical gap is the least distinct-prime support allowing violation and the best global ratio on the preceding support layer. This theorem proves the exact sharp constant 384/385 with a complete infinite equality family, while an exhibited six-prime counterexample makes the support threshold best possible. It goes beyond the prior even-two/odd-four sufficient cases, including n=2310 where psi(n)>2n, and cannot be inferred from a finite counterexample list. The bound does not claim to resolve unrestricted behavior or density.
